rows.subtype: My view is the only view [Actor]
rows.description: A toddler hides his face and believes no one can see him, or shows a picture facing himself. He cannot yet imagine that others see differently.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A preschooler assumes his parents know what he saw at school and gives puzzling half-stories. He also thinks everyone shares his feelings and wants.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A caregiver asks what the other child might feel, uses pictures and pretend play, and models saying how others see things, so empathy and viewpoint-taking grow.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: An older child begins to understand that friends may believe or want different things, but still struggles when his own strong feelings are involved.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17

rows.description: A teenager feels that his experiences are unique, that nobody has felt this before, and that everyone is watching him. It gradually softens as he meets more people.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12

rows.description: A parent or teacher recognises that a teenager's self-focus is a normal stage, listens without dismissing the feelings, and gently widens the viewpoint over time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12

rows.description: A child insists the cracked cup was never cracked and that they did not spill anything, as if the fact will vanish if unsaid; fear of being in trouble outweighs the wish to be accurate.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child whose parent has lost a job keeps saying everything is fine and stops asking questions; not knowing feels safer than facing the worry, though tension leaks out as poor sleep and short temper.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Facing a bad result in small doses [Response]
rows.description: A teenager who denied a poor result learns to say the fact aloud to one trusted person first and then plan; denial softened the shock, but acceptance in small doses lets action begin.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student sees falling marks and unpaid fees yet says it will sort itself out and skips the counsellor's email; dread is managed by not looking until a deadline forces the issue.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
